guidance: Compare designs at the same impedance and cutoff. The ladder here is ideal: a wound inductor behaves close to its value at HF, but at UHF its self-resonance and the capacitors’ ESL set the real curve.
method: The element values are the low-pass prototype g-values, denormalised to the cutoff frequency fc and the termination impedance Z0. Butterworth uses g(k) = 2 sin((2k - 1) pi / 2n), whose amplitude response is 1 / sqrt(1 + (f/fc)^2n), maximally flat and 3.01 dB down at fc. Chebyshev type I uses the ladder recursion g(1) = 2 a(1) / gamma and g(k) = 4 a(k-1) a(k) / (b(k-1) g(k-1)) with gamma = sinh(beta / 2n), beta = ln(coth(ripple / 17.37)), a(k) = sin((2k - 1) pi / 2n) and b(k) = gamma^2 + sin^2(k pi / n), so the ripple at the cutoff equals the ripple entered and the 3 dB point sits at fc cosh(acosh(1/eps) / n) with eps = sqrt(10^(ripple/10) - 1). The series elements are L = g Z0 / (2 pi fc) and the shunt elements C = g / (2 pi fc Z0), alternating series inductor first; the mirrored network that starts with the capacitor has the same response. Attenuation is read from the components themselves: each series arm contributes the transmission matrix [[1, jwL], [0, 1]] and each shunt arm [[1, 0], [j wC, 1]], and |S21| = 2 / |A + B/Z0 + C Z0 + D| over the cascade, which reproduces the closed-form response to better than 0.001 dB and therefore checks the element values rather than restating them. The order a target needs inverts the response: n = log10(10^(A/10) - 1) / (2 log10(fs/fc)) for Butterworth, and n = acosh(sqrt((10^(A/10) - 1) / eps^2)) / acosh(fs/fc) for Chebyshev, rounded up. Even-order Chebyshev prototypes need a load termination of coth^2(beta/4) times the source, which a symmetrically terminated ladder cannot present without coupled coils, so Chebyshev is offered in odd orders only. Ranges: order 1 to 8, cutoff 0.1 to 5000 MHz, impedance 1 to 1000 ohms, stopband edge 1.01 to 100 times the cutoff, ripple 0.01 to 3 dB and target 0.1 to 120 dB. Parts are ideal and lossless: winding resistance, inductor self-resonance, capacitor ESL, tolerances and temperature drift are not modelled, and elliptic, Bessel and band transforms are not offered. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
